text: Weekly shop just hit $280 for a family of four. I swear the same trolley was $190 two years ago. Anyone actually found a way to cut this that isn't just buying the home brand of everything?
Sparky here. Spent Sunday night doing quotes and chasing three invoices that are 60 days overdue. The tools part of the job is easy. It's the paperwork that wears you down.
Saw 14 pitches this week. 11 were 'AI for X' with no customer who'd pay for it. The 3 I'm following up all had one thing in common: they'd already sold it to someone, even manually.
Cancelled four subscriptions this month. Streaming, a meal kit, a fitness app and something I don't even remember signing up for. Felt great. Not adding anything new unless it saves me money.
Working on a piece about Aussie startups solving cost-of-living problems. Not interested in press releases. Looking for founders whose customers will actually talk to me. DMs open.
Running a cafe in Newcastle. Energy bill up 30%, rent up again, and two staff left for the mines. Every 'business app' I've tried wants $49 a month to do something I can do in a notebook.
Reminder for anyone launching a subscription product: if it's easy to sign up, it needs to be just as easy to cancel. Hidden auto-renewals are the most common complaint we see.
Out here in regional Queensland the internet drops out every time it rains. Half these new apps assume you've got 5G and a Woolies down the road. We don't.
Every year someone tells us they'll disrupt Australian retail. Most forget we have two supermarkets because the logistics across this country are brutal. Solve that and I'll listen.
Uni student budget update: rent $260 a week for a room, groceries $60, and I still need a laptop that doesn't die mid-lecture. Any app that helps me split costs with housemates, I'm in.
Retired last year. My grandson set up three apps on my phone and I can't work out any of them. If it needs a 10-step tutorial, it's not for me. Just make the button bigger.
Unpopular opinion: Australia is a great test market but a hard one to scale in. 27M people. If your plan is AU only, show me why it still makes money. If not, show me the next market.
Ops manager at a mid-size logistics firm. We use 11 different systems and none of them talk to each other. Whoever fixes that for under the cost of one more admin hire wins.
My followers ask me every week for ways to save on bills. The ones that go viral are always dead simple: one thing, one number, one tip. Nobody shares a 'platform'.
Mum of three. School lunches, sport rego, uniforms, excursions. I need one place that tells me what's due this week and what it costs. Not another newsletter.
Not trying anything new with my data after the last two big breaches. My licence number is out there twice now. Prove you're safe first, then we can talk.
Collecting more personal information than you need is not a growth strategy. If your app needs my date of birth to recommend a coffee, expect questions.
We partner with about 5 startups a year. The ones that work fit into what our customers already do. The ones that fail ask our customers to change their habits.
Software dev in Melbourne. Happy to pay for good tools, but there's a weird gap here: lots of US apps that don't know what GST or Medicare is. Build for Aussies and I'll try it.
Own a small salon in Perth. No-shows cost me about $400 a week. I've tried deposits, reminders, everything. Still happens. Honestly would pay to make this go away.
